svg.title: Norm convergence yields convergence in measure and a subsequence with almost-everywhere convergence, but not full-sequence pointwise convergence
svg.desc: A three-stage descending path starts with convergence in the square-integrable norm, continues to convergence in measure, and reaches a strictly increasing subsequence whose chosen representatives converge almost everywhere. A blocked path from norm convergence directly to almost-everywhere convergence of the full sequence marks the theorem that is not available. The final pointwise Birkhoff theorem remains beyond a maximal closure step.
svg.text: Three valid implications stop before the full pointwise theorem
The quantifier over a chosen subsequence cannot be erased.
Norm convergence alone does not certify almost-everywhere convergence of every term in the full sequence.
A sequence may be small in norm while exceptional sets move from one index to the next.
Use the weak maximal estimate to close pointwise convergence beyond the dense good core.
Takeaway: mean convergence finds a limit in function space; a maximal argument must still control moving exceptional sets.
